requirement: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project: every `.rs` file except those under `.git` or `target` directories at any depth or under the project-root `book`, `evidence`, or `vendor` directories. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:none` under {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
rationale:
**Judgment:** `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` is implemented and tested. I found no unmarked implementation and no unspecified behavior.

**Implementation**
- **Hook-up.** `inspect_repository_with_progress` (src/evidence.rs) calls `crate::rust_coverage::validate_rust_functions` during repository validation. It passes the shared `errors` and `discovery_errors` lists, so a Rust finding or parse failure is a validation error and also a discovery error.
- **File selection.** `rust_files` (src/rust_coverage.rs) walks every directory and collects each `.rs` file.
  - It skips `.git` and `target` directories at any depth.
  - It skips `book`, `evidence`, and `vendor` only when the directory is the project root (`directory == root`).
  - Unreadable directories, entries, and files are reported, not silently skipped.
- **Parsing and parse failures.** `missing_function_references` parses each file with `outline::parse_with(&RUST_PROFILE, ..)`. `check_errors` in the outline module turns any tree-sitter error or missing node into an `OutlineError`. `validate_rust_functions` reports that as `file:line: cannot parse Rust source: ...`, so a parse failure is never skipped.
- **Item kinds.** `KINDS` in src/outline/rust.rs maps `function_item` and `function_signature_item` to `fn`. The signature kind covers bodiless trait methods. It maps `struct_item`, `enum_item`, and `union_item` to their own kinds. The coverage check keeps only `fn`, `struct`, `enum`, and `union` nodes.
- **What counts as a reference.**
  - Only comments that the outline assigns to a node count. That assignment is done by the outline code under `outline_comments`; the requirement delegates it there.
  - A comment in a string or char literal is not a comment, so it never counts.
  - A reference on an enclosing `mod` or `impl` does not reach the items inside it.
  - Fenced `habeas:none` citations count only when `builtin.check` accepts them and the fence is closed.
  - A `{cite}` or `{test}` of an example counts only if `example_references_requirement` finds a reference to a real requirement. A reference to a term never counts.
  - `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` to requirements all count, and unknown names do not.
- **Reporting.** Each unreferenced item is reported as `label:line: kind name has no requirement or example citation`, giving file, line, kind, and name.
- **Marking.** Each function that implements part of the requirement carries an `{impl}` marker:
  - `inspect_repository_with_progress`
  - `example_references_requirement`
  - `missing_function_references`
  - `rust_files`
  - `validate_rust_functions`
  - `display_path`
  - `OutlineNode::display_name`

  Other helpers (`comments`, the literal scanners) are marked with `definitions.dependencies`, which specifies that behavior. I found no behavior in the `{impl}` code that this requirement leaves unspecified.

**Tests**
- **Item cases.** `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references` covers:
  - enclosing `mod` and `impl` references that do not count;
  - string, raw-string, and char literals;
  - unknown requirements;
  - body comments;
  - a comment run across a blank line;
  - trailing comments;
  - inner doc comments (`//!`);
  - outer doc comments.

  `checks_trait_test_helper_and_nested_functions_separately` covers trait methods, nested functions, test helpers, and `{test}` references. `locates_functions_after_unicode_text` covers line numbers after non-ASCII text.
- **Struct, enum, and union.** `structs_enums_and_unions_need_references_attached_or_inside` covers attached references, references before a field or variant, references before attributes, and nested structs.
- **Examples.** `an_example_counts_only_when_it_references_a_requirement` covers an example with `{cite}`, one with `{test}`, an orphan example, an example that only cites another example, an example that only cites a term, and an `{impl}` of a term.
- **File selection and parse failures.** `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures` covers:
  - skipping `target`, `.git`, and the root `book`, `evidence`, and `vendor` directories;
  - still scanning `src/vendor` and `src/book`;
  - reporting a parse failure.
- **Builtin and fence cases.** `fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated` in tests/references.rs covers `habeas:none` as an inline citation, with an empty body, with the wrong role, and unclosed. It also covers an unknown built-in.
- **End to end.** tests/authoring_batch.rs (`discovery_errors_fail_before_configuration_or_inference`) and tests/commands.rs (`status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form`) check that parse failures and findings surface in `author` and `status`.

The only untested paths are I/O failures such as unreadable files or directories. They are simple error-reporting branches, so I do not count them as a gap.

text: :::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project: every `.rs` file except those under `.git` or `target` directories at any depth or under the project-root `book`, `evidence`, or `vendor` directories. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:none` under {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
:::{req} no_requirement
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:none` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this only when no requirement or example applies to the item under the
> reference procedure. The citation MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST
> justify why the item exists. An item with an invariant worth checking, such as
> a cache that must not change results, needs a requirement stating that
> invariant instead. An item citing this MUST NOT implement end-user-observable
> behavior that no requirement specifies.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it. Validation MUST report an inline citation of it
or a fenced citation whose body, without comment delimiters and other
references, is empty. Whether the justification holds MUST be assessed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. `habeas status --all` MUST list
each `habeas:none` citation with its item and justification.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} definition

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.targets`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
